subject: Hosted suitability and quickstart follow-up
raw_messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@cartly.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted suitability and quickstart follow-up

Samir — thanks again for the call and demo earlier. Quick recap and three asks so we can size a hosted pilot for Cartly:

1) Recap: You showed chat+classification flows for the support routing use case. We discussed Hosted API for quick evaluation vs Dedicated capacity if you need strict isolation or predictable sustained throughput.

2) Need from you: a couple capacity details so we can provision sandbox endpoints and propose rate bands:
   - Peak QPS (external API calls) and typical sustained QPS
   - Typical input+output token lengths per request (or example prompt sizes)
   - Any regulatory/data residency constraints (do you need a VPC or on-prem?)

3) Proposed immediate plan: we can spin up a hosted sandbox (chat endpoint + embeddings endpoint) and provision a trial rate cap. That gives Cartly a quick way to validate latency, quality, and cost without committing to Dedicated. If you confirm sustained throughput >500 QPS or need network isolation, we’ll recommend Dedicated or Private.

I attached a short Redwood quickstart (redwood-quickstart-hosted.pdf) and a lightweight deployment worksheet we can fill together.

Can you reply with the capacity answers above and suggest 30 minutes later this week for a quick on-call to agree rate bands?

Thanks — Avery
Avery Johnson
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: redwood-quickstart-hosted.pdf (1 page guide)
Attachment: cartly-deployment-proposal.xlsx (worksheet)

From: Samir Patel <samir@cartly.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Lin <rachel@cartly.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 15:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted suitability and quickstart follow-up

Avery — thanks for the follow-up and for the quickstart PDF. Answers below and some clarifying Qs: 

- Peak external QPS: ~150 requests/sec (we see short spikes during ticket surges), sustained average ~35–45 req/sec.
- Typical tokens: ~250 tokens in + ~100 tokens out on average (we have handful of 1k+ token aggregation reports but rare).
- Data residency: must remain in us-east region; not a hard requirement to be VPC/on-prem today but may be required later for enterprise customers.

Clarifying questions:
- Do hosted sandboxes support per-endpoint rate caps and separate API keys for dev vs prod?
- How do you recommend we map features (ticket classification, summary, embeddings) to endpoints for the trial?
- Any soft limits we should plan for on concurrent connections?

We’re cost conscious — if hosted is clearly cheaper for our eval workload that’s preferable. Happy to do a 30-min call Wed or Thu afternoon.

— Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Product, Cartly
samir@cartly.com | +1 (646) 555-0199

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Hosted suitability and quickstart follow-up (Cartly)

Marissa / Jordan — forwarding Samir’s answers from Cartly. Short summary and recommendation for internal ops pickup:

Summary:
- Peak: ~150 QPS, sustained 35–45 QPS
- Typical tokens: ~350 total / occasional long requests (~1k tokens)
- Data residency: requires us-east region; VPC not required immediately

Recommendation (hosted-first path):
- Provision hosted sandbox with two sandbox API keys (dev/prod mimic) scoped to separate endpoints.
- Create endpoints: chat-support-v1 (primary), classify-ticket-v1 (lighter), embeddings-lookup-v1 (for vector store experiments).
- Initial trial rate bands: soft cap 200 QPS per account, 60 concurrent connections limit; we can tighten if infra sees issues.  Offer prefix/KV caching guidance to reduce peak tokens.
- Canary routing + automatic fallback to a smaller model variant if latency >500ms for production rollout testing.

Action items:
- Jordan: can you provision sandbox endpoints in us-east and create two API keys? Include ratecaps per-key as above.
- Marissa: please prepare SE notes (prefetch/prefix cache suggestions + prompt templates) and sync with UX to capture expected prompt sizes.
- I’ll schedule a 30-min sync with Samir + Rachel after endpoints are ready.

Thoughts? If they later need sustained >500 QPS or strict network isolation we recommend moving to Dedicated or Private.

Thanks — Avery

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@cartly.com>
Cc: Rachel Lin <rachel@cartly.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted suitability and quickstart follow-up

Samir — great, thanks for the numbers and the timing. We’ll do the hosted sandbox path to get you moving quickly. Next steps (short):

1) We’ll provision hosted sandbox (us-east) with the following endpoints and trial caps:
   - chat-support-v1: soft cap 200 QPS, 60 concurrent connections
   - classify-ticket-v1: soft cap 100 QPS
   - embeddings-lookup-v1: soft cap 20 QPS
   Keys: two sandbox API keys (dev / staging mimic) with separate quotas.

2) SE deliverables (attached): a short prompt-template pack and a deployment worksheet (cartly-deployment-proposal.xlsx). I attached the worksheet and the quickstart PDF.

3) Proposed follow-up: 30 min Wednesday 10/14 at 11:00 AM ET — confirm if that works for you (Rachel can join). We’ll walk through the endpoints, rate caps, and prefetched cache options.

FAQ / quick answers to your earlier questions:
- Yes: hosted sandboxes support per-endpoint caps and multiple API keys for separate environments.
- Mapping suggestion: put heavier context summarization on chat-support-v1, synchronous classification on classify-ticket-v1, and offline/upsert workflows to embeddings-lookup-v1.
- Concurrency: the soft limits above should be fine for an eval; we’ll monitor and bump if needed during the trial.

If that plan looks good I’ll ask Jordan to provision and share creds, and Marissa will send the prompt templates.

Thanks — Avery
Avery Johnson
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwood.com
